# Forecast ledger: China youth unemployment, small models against a naive benchmark

*Generated by `make_readme.py` from `results/rolling_origin.json`, `ledger.csv` and `results/scoreboard.md`. Do not edit by hand.*

## Puzzle

Can a model with very few adjustable numbers forecast the official youth unemployment rate in China better than the rule "next month will look like the same month a year ago"? An earlier model in this repository (`engine/firms/`) had 11 fitted parameters, and an internal review found it lost to that rule out of sample. This folder replaces it for research with a few small models, each explainable in a sentence or two, scored on many forecast origins, plus a public ledger of forecasts frozen before the data arrive.

## Fact check

The series is the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) urban surveyed unemployment rate for ages 16-24, percent, monthly. It has two definitions:

- Old method (students who are looking for work are counted): 66 months in the data file, 2018-01 to 2023-06. The data file holds no old-method values after that.
- New method (students excluded): from 2023-12 to 2026-09. This is the only series used for evaluation, because the two definitions give different levels and are not comparable.

The new-method series spans 34 calendar months and holds 32 observations; 2026-03, 2026-04 are not in the data file. That is short: every number below rests on few forecasts, and the counts are given beside each number. The values are used exactly as stored in `engine/firms/data_china.py` (copied to `data/observed.csv`); they were not re-checked against NBS pages for this folder. Annual graduating-class sizes are the Ministry of Education's announced expected classes (`data/graduates.csv`).

## Rival forecasters

| Name | Estimated numbers | In plain words |
|---|---:|---|
| `naive_same_month` | 0 | The forecast is the rate for the same calendar month a year earlier. Nothing is estimated. This is the benchmark. |
| `naive_last` | 0 | The forecast is the most recent observed rate, whatever month is being forecast. Nothing is estimated. |
| `seasonal_drift` | 1 | Same month a year earlier, plus the average year-on-year change over the last 6 months. One number is estimated (the average change); the window of 6 is fixed in advance. |
| `seasonal_profile` | 4 | A smooth yearly shape (2 sine-cosine pairs, so 4 estimated numbers, fitted to all data up to the origin) added to a level set by the average of the last 12 months with the shape removed. The level is set by a rule, not fitted. A free 12-month profile would be 11 numbers, so it is shrunk to 2 pairs. |
| `graduate_inflow` | 2 | Same month a year earlier, plus a shift that depends on how much bigger the graduating class is than the year before (percent growth). Two numbers are estimated: a constant shift and a slope on cohort growth, by least squares on past year-on-year changes. A class counts as known from December of the year before it graduates. |

Each model is limited to four estimated numbers or fewer. The benchmark is `naive_same_month`.

## The test fixed in advance

- Forecast origins: every observed month of the new-method series up to 2026-08. At each origin a model sees only data up to that month (tested in `test_ledger.py`).
- Horizons: 1, 3, 6, 12 months ahead. A forecast is scored only if the target month was observed.
- Score: mean absolute error in percentage points, and for each model the paired difference against `naive_same_month` on the same origin-target pairs (model absolute error minus benchmark absolute error; negative means the model was closer), the share of pairs the model won, and a paired t statistic.
- Each model is compared on the pairs where both it and the benchmark can forecast, so the number of pairs differs between rows. Models that need more history start later.
- The rule, the horizons and the benchmark were fixed before the results were produced. No model was tuned after seeing the scores.

## Results

No forecaster beat naive_same_month across the board. In 3 of 15 model-horizon comparisons the model had a lower mean absolute error than naive_same_month: seasonal_drift at 1 month (n = 16, mean difference -0.15, t = -1.04); graduate_inflow at 1 month (n = 13, mean difference -0.09, t = -0.84); graduate_inflow at 6 months (n = 8, mean difference -0.09, t = -0.69). In the other 12 it had a higher error or an identical one.

None of the comparisons in the model's favour has a paired t of -2 or lower, so none is distinguishable from noise at this sample size.

Notes on reading the table. The benchmark row compares itself with itself. `naive_last` at 12 months gives the same forecast as the benchmark by construction. Consecutive origins overlap, so pairs are not independent and the t statistics are, if anything, too optimistic. A blank or n/a t means fewer than three pairs or no variation.

nothing to score yet: no ledger target month has an observation in data/observed.csv.

## What this does and does not show

It shows how often each small model came closer than `naive_same_month` over the origins available, and by how much, on a series of 32 observations. It does not show that any model captures how the labour market works: a model that matches the seasonal pattern says nothing about causes. The cohort model has two estimated numbers identified from 3 graduating classes (2024 to 2026) at the last origin, so its slope on cohort growth is weakly pinned down. Differences smaller than the error of the data series itself cannot be read as skill. The ledger is the real test: the forecasts were frozen before the months they predict were published.

## How to add a new month and rescore

1. Append one row to `data/observed.csv`: `year,month,rate,source_note` (rate in percent, new method; write where the number came from in `source_note`). When a new graduating class is announced, append it to `data/graduates.csv`.
2. Run `python score.py`. It reads `ledger.csv` and `data/observed.csv`, refits nothing, and writes `results/scoreboard.md` and `results/scoreboard.csv`. With no new months it prints "nothing to score yet".
3. Optionally re-run `python evaluate.py` and `python make_readme.py` to refresh the rolling-origin results and this page. `ledger.csv` is append-only; do not change frozen rows. New freezes should be added as new rows with their own freeze date and data cutoff.
4. Run `python -m unittest test_ledger` to check the no-leak guard, the ledger rows and the scorer.

## Limits

- Short series: 32 observations, with 2026-03, 2026-04 missing. The 12-month horizon rests on the fewest pairs.
- Missing months inside the span are filled by straight-line interpolation only when a model reads them as a reference; scoring uses real observations only.
- A graduating class is treated as known from December of the year before it graduates. This is an assumption about announcement timing that was not checked against the dates of the announcements.
- Data values come from `engine/firms/data_china.py` as stored; their provenance flags are described there. They were not independently re-verified for this folder.
- The new-method definition may change again; if it does, the series breaks and the ledger scores should say so.
- Seasonal and cohort models fitted on about two years of data cannot tell a stable seasonal shape from a one-off pattern.
- The earlier blind forecast was frozen with a different model, a different cutoff and a different benchmark, so it is scored against both its own benchmark and `naive_same_month` in the scoreboard.
